mainTopic: Why the חכמים require a בית דין for a שבועת העדות taken מפי עצמו: is it a dispute about דון מינה ומינה, or a קל וחומר limited by דיו?
overview: This amud finishes one discussion and then starts a new משנה about שבועת העדות. First, רב פפא explains why the חכמים say an oath taken on one's own counts only in בית דין. He says they learn it through a קל וחומר, and the rule of דיו limits that קל וחומר to בית דין. The other חכמים push back with a משנה about שבועת הפקדון. רב פפא agrees that the פקדון משנה involves the דון מינה ומינה dispute, but says our משנה does not. Next the גמרא explains three lines of the משנה. A ברייתא learns from the missing word ״וְנֶעְלַם״ that one is liable even for lying on purpose. רב explains what counts as a 'mistaken' oath. The גמרא then shows why רב's ruling about רב כהנא and רב אסי was still needed. A new משנה describes how a שבועת העדות happens and gives rules for repeated oaths, two witnesses, and two sets of witnesses. The גמרא opens with שמואל's ruling that witnesses are exempt until the plaintiff himself asks them, and starts to challenge it. The challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב פפא: Learning from פקדון Would Leave No Room for Dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that if the חכמים really learned from פקדון, everyone would agree to borrow all its details, so the dispute cannot be explained that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to them: If the חכמים learn this law from the oath about a deposit, then everyone agrees we take all the details from there.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא is rejecting the earlier idea that the חכמים and רבי מאיר argue about דון מינה ומינה. He says that if the source were פקדון, there would be no argument at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שבועת הפקדון, someone who swears on his own is liable even outside בית דין. If the חכמים learned שבועת העדות from פקדון, they would have to borrow that detail too, and then they could not require בית דין. So their source must be something else.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit left with a guardian; here it means the oath a guardian takes about it (שבועת הפקדון).
Learn from it, and from it: once you borrow a law from a source, you take all of that source's details.
From his own mouth: he swears on his own, without being put under oath by others.

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying the חכמים agree with רבי מאיר. He is saying that their source is not פקדון, so the reason for their view must lie elsewhere.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to them:
If the Rabbis learn it from the deposit oath,
phrases.notes: "It" is the case of a witness who takes the oath of testimony on his own.

phrases.english: then everyone would not disagree
that we learn from it, and from it.
phrases.notes: Learning "from it, and from it" means you copy every detail of the source case, including the detail that no בית דין is needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב פָּפָּא: אִי מִפִּקָּדוֹן גָּמְרִי לַהּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the earlier explanation of the dispute, which was given just before this part of the text.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the dispute is about דון מינה ומינה versus a more limited borrowing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If the source were פקדון, borrowing all its details would force even the חכמים to say no בית דין is needed.

steps.title: The חכמים' Real Source: A קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the חכמים learn liability for swearing on one's own through a קל וחומר from being put under oath by others.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is the חכמים' reason: they bring it through a קל וחומר. If he is liable when others put him under oath, then when he swears on his own, surely he is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives his own explanation of where the חכמים get their law. Their source is a קל וחומר inside שבועת העדות itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being put under oath by others (מפי אחרים) creates liability. Swearing on one's own seems even stronger, so it should surely create liability too. This logic comes from within שבועת העדות, not from פקדון.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger one: if X is true here, it is surely true there.
From the mouth of others: someone else puts him under oath and he answers "אמן".

phrases.english: Rather, this is the reason of the Rabbis:
that they bring it by a kal vachomer:
If from the mouth of others he is liable,
from his own mouth, all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting פקדון as the source, רב פפא offers a different source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים derive liability for an oath taken מפי עצמו through a קל וחומר from an oath taken מפי אחרים.

steps.title: דיו Limits the קל וחומר to בית דין
steps.stepSummary: Because the law comes from a קל וחומר, the rule of דיו limits it: just like the oath מפי אחרים, the oath מפי עצמו counts only in בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they derive it from a קל וחומר, the derived case can be no stronger than its source. Someone put under oath by others is liable in court but not outside court. So too, someone who swears on his own is liable before a court but not outside a court.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his explanation. The rule of דיו is the reason the חכמים require בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A law learned through a קל וחומר cannot go further than its source (דיו לבא מן הדין להיות כנדון). The source case, an oath מפי אחרים, works only in בית דין. So the derived case, an oath מפי עצמו, also works only in בית דין.

keyTerms.term: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
keyTerms.meaning: It is enough for what comes from the argument to be like its source: a קל וחומר cannot produce more than its source has.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, the חכמים require בית דין for an oath מפי עצמו because of דיו on a קל וחומר, not because of how much they borrow from פקדון.

phrases.english: And since they bring it from a kal vachomer,

phrases.aramaic: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן:
phrases.english: it is enough for what comes from the argument to be like its source:
Just as one put under oath by others:

phrases.aramaic: בְּבֵית דִּין אִין, שֶׁלֹּא בְּבֵית דִּין לָא;
phrases.english: in court, yes; not in court, no;
so too one under oath from his own mouth:

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין אִין, שֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין לָא.
phrases.english: before a court, yes; not before a court, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּמַיְיתוּ לַהּ מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר – דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the limiting rule of דיו to the קל וחומר from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of דיו, an oath מפי עצמו creates liability only before a בית דין, just like an oath מפי אחרים.

steps.title: The Rabbis Challenge רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רב פפא how he can say the dispute is not about דון מינה ומינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים said to רב פפא: How can you say that they do not disagree about דון מינה ומינה?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים of the study hall attack רב פפא's claim from step 1. This line sets up the source they are about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said everyone agrees to דון מינה ומינה. The challengers think there is evidence that רבי מאיר and the חכמים do argue about exactly this kind of borrowing.

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rav Pappa:
Can you really say
that they do not disagree about "learn from it and from it"?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב פָּפָּא: מִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's claim from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that everyone agrees to דון מינה ומינה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about פקדון seems to show the same two sides arguing about which details pass between שבועת הפקדון and שבועת העדות.

steps.title: The משנה About the Deposit Oath
steps.stepSummary: The challengers quote the משנה on שבועת הפקדון. רבי מאיר requires בית דין for an oath מפי אחרים, while the חכמים say any denial makes him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't we learn about a deposit: The deposit oath applies to men and women, to non-relatives and relatives, to those fit to testify and those unfit, before a court and not before a court, when he swears on his own. But when others put him under oath, he is not liable until he denies it in court. This is רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים say: whether on his own or from others, once he denied it, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the source behind the challenge in step 4. It is a משנה where רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about whether בית דין is needed in שבועת הפקדון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here, in פקדון, רבי מאיר adds a requirement of בית דין for an oath מפי אחרים, a detail that fits שבועת העדות. The חכמים do not add it. So the same two sides seem to argue about how far details carry over between the two oaths, and this undercuts רב פפא.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the sides flip. Here in פקדון it is רבי מאיר who requires בית דין (for an oath מפי אחרים), and the חכמים who say any denial makes him liable.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn about a deposit:
The deposit oath applies to men and to women,
to non-relatives and to relatives,
to those fit and to those unfit,
phrases.notes: Fit or unfit to be witnesses. Unlike the oath of testimony, the deposit oath does not depend on being a valid witness.

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין וְשֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין –
phrases.english: before a court and not before a court,
when it is from his own mouth;
and from the mouth of others he is not liable
until he denies it in court.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִפִּי עַצְמוֹ וּבֵין מִפִּי אֲחֵרִים –
phrases.english: whether from his own mouth or from the mouth of others,
once he denied it, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן גַּבֵּי פִּקָּדוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text behind the challenge in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר and the חכמים do argue about how far the details of one oath carry over to the other, which goes against רב פפא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on שבועת הפקדון: רבי מאיר requires בית דין for an oath מפי אחרים, while the חכמים make him liable for any denial.

steps.title: The Challengers Finish Their Challenge From the Deposit Case
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים must have learned the liability of מושבע מפי אחרים בפקדון from שבועת העדות, yet they do not require בית דין. So they do argue about דון מינה ומינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do the חכמים get the rule that a person put under oath by others about a deposit is liable? Don't they learn it from the oath of testimony? So we can conclude that they argue about דון מינה ומינה.
steps.whatsHappening: The challengers finish the proof they started in Step 5. They show that the חכמים' ruling in the פקדון case only works if the חכמים hold דון מינה ואוקי באתרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not mention an oath מפי אחרים for a פקדון, so the חכמים must borrow it from שבועת העדות, where it is written. In עדות that oath counts only in בית דין, but the חכמים say any denial counts. So they borrow the main rule but not its details, and this is exactly the דון מינה ומינה dispute that רב פפא tried to deny.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do they know it?
Learn from a source and take all its details too

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים here hold the opposite of דון מינה ומינה. They learn the rule from עדות but leave the בית דין detail behind, which is called דון מינה ואוקי באתרה.

phrases.english: One who is put under oath by others regarding a deposit
from where do the Rabbis know that he is liable?
Is it not that they learn it from the oath of testimony?
So conclude from this
that they argue about whether we learn a rule from a source together with all its details?

steps.triggerLanguage: מושבע מפי אחרים בפקדון מנא להו לרבנן דחייב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the משנה quoted in Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim (Steps 1–3) that the dispute is not about דון מינה ומינה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים can only get מפי אחרים for a פקדון from עדות, but they drop the בית דין detail. So they reject דון מינה ומינה, and the dispute with רבי מאיר is about exactly that.

steps.title: רב פפא Agrees About That משנה but Not About Ours
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא admits the פקדון משנה shows a דון מינה ומינה dispute. He says our משנה about שבועת העדות proves nothing, since there the חכמים can rely on a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: From that משנה, yes, you can learn it. From this one, there is nothing to learn.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge. He gives in about the פקדון משנה but keeps his explanation of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פקדון case there is no other way to get the rule, so the dispute really is about דון מינה ומינה. In our משנה, about an oath taken on one's own, the חכמים can learn through a קל וחומר with דיו, as he said in Steps 2–3. So our משנה does not have to involve that dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: There is nothing to learn from it

steps.whatToRemember: Both משניות can stand together. In the פקדון case the dispute is about דון מינה ומינה. In our משנה the חכמים may simply be using a קל וחומר limited by דיו.

phrases.english: From that one, yes;
phrases.notes: He means the פקדון משנה just quoted. That one really does show the דון מינה ומינה dispute.

phrases.english: from this one, there is nothing to learn from it.
phrases.notes: He means our משנה about שבועת העדות, where the קל וחומר from Step 2 is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: מההיא אין מהא ליכא למשמע מינה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6 by limiting how far it reaches
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial concession and separating the two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פקדון משנה proves that the dispute in our משנה is also about דון מינה ומינה
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the פקדון משנה involves דון מינה ומינה. Our משנה can be explained with a קל וחומר and דיו.

steps.title: Source for Liability on an Intentional False Oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that one is liable for an intentional false oath of testimony and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one is liable for swearing falsely on purpose. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line in the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a קרבן is brought only for a sin done by mistake, so a קרבן for a deliberate false oath is surprising. The גמרא wants to know what in the תורה teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: And one is liable for an intentional oath.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: וחייבין על זדון השבועה מנהני מילי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the פסוקים for bringing a קרבן on a deliberate false oath of testimony

steps.title: The Missing Word ״ונעלם״ Teaches Liability Even on Purpose
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא notes that the other cases of the קרבן say ״וְנֶעְלַם״ but שבועת העדות does not. This teaches that one is liable whether he sinned on purpose or by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught in a ברייתא: in all the other cases the תורה says ״וְנֶעְלַם״, "and it is hidden," but here it does not. This makes one liable for doing it on purpose just as for doing it by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 8 with a ברייתא that learns from a missing word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״וְנֶעְלַם״ means the person did not realize what he was doing, so it limits those cases to mistakes. Since this word is missing in the פסוק about שבועת העדות, that limit does not apply, and even someone who denies on purpose brings the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: "And it is hidden" (he did not realize)

steps.whyThisMatters: This makes שבועת העדות unusual among the sins that bring a קרבן: the קרבן applies even when he sinned on purpose.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
In all of them it says "and it is hidden,"
phrases.notes: "All of them" are the other cases of this קרבן: becoming טמא and swearing about one's own actions. ויקרא 5:2–4.

phrases.english: but here it does not say "and it is hidden";
to make one liable for doing it on purpose just as for doing it by mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: דתנו רבנן בכולן נאמר בהן ונעלם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since the פסוק about שבועת העדות leaves out ״ונעלם״, one is liable on purpose just as by mistake

steps.title: What Is an Unintentional Oath With Intentional Denial?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of an unintentional oath together with intentional denial of testimony and asks what it looks like.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said one is liable for an unintentional oath together with intentional denial of testimony. What does such a case look like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and asks for a real-life picture of it. This sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems hard to picture. If the person knows he has testimony and is lying on purpose, in what way is his oath a mistake? The גמרא asks what he could be unaware of.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the case look like?

phrases.english: And for its unintentional form together with intentional denial of the testimony.
phrases.notes: Another quote from our משנה. He knows he has testimony, but the oath is still called a mistake.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances of
an unintentional oath together with intentional denial of the testimony?

steps.triggerLanguage: ועל שגגתה עם זדון העדות היכי דמי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete case where the oath counts as a mistake but the denial of testimony is on purpose

steps.title: He Knows It Is Forbidden but Not That It Brings a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב: the case is someone who knows the oath is forbidden but does not know that it requires a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: it is a person who says, "I know this oath is forbidden, but I do not know whether one has to bring a קרבן for it or not."
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question from Step 10 by describing what the person does not know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He denies the testimony on purpose and even knows that swearing falsely is forbidden. His only mistake is not knowing that the oath requires a קרבן, and that alone makes the oath count as unintentional.

keyTerms.meaning: One must bring a קרבן for it

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, a person who knows the oath is forbidden but does not know it requires a קרבן counts as making the oath by mistake.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
It is a case of one who says: "I know that this oath is forbidden,"
but I do not know

phrases.aramaic: אִם חַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ קׇרְבָּן אִם לֹא״.
phrases.english: whether or not one must bring a קרבן for it."

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יהודה אמר רב באומר יודע אני ששבועה זו אסורה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The person knows the oath is forbidden but does not know it requires a קרבן

steps.title: Does our משנה already teach רב's ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that there is no liability for an oath that was 'unwitting alone.' It asks whether this already teaches רב's ruling about רב כהנא and רב אסי, which would make רב's statement unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And they are not liable when the mistake is only about the testimony itself.' Shall we say we already learned here the ruling רב gave about רב כהנא and רב אסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and points out that it seems to say the same thing רב said in an earlier story. It is setting up a question about why רב needed to say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'plain' שוגג means the witness truly forgot that he knows anything. The משנה says he is exempt. רב said the same about רב כהנא and רב אסי, who each swore they were right and one turned out to be wrong. If the משנה already teaches this, רב's ruling seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: a 'plain' mistake: he did not even know his oath was false
'Shall we say we already learned it?' This suggests a later statement is not needed

phrases.english: And they are not liable for its unwitting form alone.
phrases.notes: גְּרֵידְתָּא means plain or bare. He really forgot he knows the testimony, so he never knew he was lying.

phrases.english: Shall we say we have already learned
that of Rav Kahana and Rav Asi?
phrases.notes: He means רב's ruling in their story earlier (on 26a): the one who swore and was wrong is exempt, since he believed he was right.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא תְּנֵינָא לִדְרַב כָּהֲנָא וּדְרַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the case of a שוגג who still brings a קרבן (step 11), the גמרא now looks at the opposite side of the משנה, the plain שוגג who is exempt, and compares it to רב's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling in the case of רב כהנא and רב אסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה already exempts a 'plain' שוגג, רב's ruling that a fully unaware swearer is exempt seems to repeat it.

steps.title: רב's ruling was still needed because of ״וְנֶעְלַם״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב's ruling was still needed. In שבועת העדות, which does not say ״וְנֶעְלַם״, the שוגג must resemble a מזיד. In שבועת ביטוי, which does say ״וְנֶעְלַם״, one might think any kind of mistake makes a person liable, so רב had to teach otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Even though the משנה teaches it, רב's ruling was needed. You might have thought: only here, by שבועת העדות, where ״וְנֶעְלַם״ is not written, the mistake must look like an intentional sin. But there, by שבועת ביטוי, where ״וְנֶעְלַם״ is written, even a complete mistake would make him liable. רב teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רב's statement was not extra. He taught it about a different kind of oath, where we might have ruled differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 we learned that שבועת העדות has no ״וְנֶעְלַם״, so a person is liable even if he lied on purpose. That means the 'mistake' case has to be close to on purpose: he knows he is lying and only does not know about the קרבן (step 11). שבועת ביטוי does say ״וְנֶעְלַם״, so one could think even total unawareness is enough to make him liable. רב teaches that even there, a person who fully believed he was telling the truth is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: even though it was taught in the משנה, it was still needed
a mistake that looks like an intentional sin: he knew he lied, but not about the קרבן
of any sort at all, even complete unawareness

steps.confusionAlert: Here הָכָא is שבועת העדות, the subject of our משנה, and הָתָם is שבועת ביטוי, the oath רב כהנא and רב אסי took. Do not mix them up.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two levels of שוגג. In one he knows he is lying but not about the קרבן; in the other he truly thinks he is telling the truth. The second kind is exempt both in שבועת העדות and, according to רב, in שבועת ביטוי.

phrases.aramaic: לָא; אַף עַל גַּב דִּתְנַן, אִיצְטְרִיךְ;
phrases.english: No; even though we learned it, it was necessary;
it would have entered your mind to say:
it is here that "and it is hidden" is not written
phrases.notes: הָכָא means שבועת העדות, the oath in our משנה.

phrases.english: so we require the unwitting case to be similar to the intentional one;
but there, where "and it is hidden" is written,
phrases.notes: הָתָם means שבועת ביטוי, the kind of oath רב כהנא and רב אסי took.

phrases.english: even any sort of unwitting mistake would make him liable;
so Rav teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; אַף עַל גַּב דִּתְנַן, אִיצְטְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 by showing that the משנה's case and רב's case are different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: different פסוקים apply to the two kinds of oath
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because שבועת ביטוי says ״וְנֶעְלַם״, one might think even total unawareness makes a person liable there.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב teaches that even in שבועת ביטוי, someone who fully believed his oath was true is exempt.

steps.title: How a שבועת העדות happens
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה describes the basic case. A man asks two witnesses to testify for him, and they deny knowing anything, either by swearing themselves or by answering ״אָמֵן״ to his oath. If they were lying, they are liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: How does a שבועת העדות work? A man said to two people, 'Come and testify for me.' They answered, 'We swear that we know no testimony for you.' Or they said, 'We know no testimony for you,' and he said, 'I make you swear,' and they said ״אָמֵן״. These witnesses are liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It shows exactly what a שבועת העדות looks like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to make the oath. The witnesses can swear by their own words, or the plaintiff can put an oath on them and they accept it by saying ״אָמֵן״. Both count as a full oath, and if they lied they bring the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: the משנה, which begins a new section
answering this to an oath counts as swearing it yourself

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that saying ״אָמֵן″ to someone else's oath counts as taking the oath, which matters for oaths in general.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The oath of testimony, how does it work?
He said to two people: "Come and testify for me";
and they answered, "An oath that we do not know any testimony for you,"
or they said to him
"We do not know any testimony for you";
and he said, "I make you swear," and they said: "Amen"
these witnesses are liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁבוּעַת הָעֵדוּת כֵּיצַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא finished explaining the previous one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who falsely deny knowing testimony, whether they swear themselves or answer ״אָמֵן״ to the plaintiff's oath, are liable.

steps.title: Five oaths outside court versus before the court
steps.stepSummary: If the plaintiff made the witnesses swear five times outside court and they later admitted in court, they are exempt. If they kept denying, they are liable for every oath. If all five oaths were in front of the court, they are liable for only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he made them swear five times outside the court, and then they came to court and admitted, they are exempt. If they denied, they are liable for each and every oath. If he made them swear five times in front of the court and they denied, they are liable only once.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a case of repeated oaths. It explains when each oath counts and when only one does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oaths outside court do not yet seal the denial. If the witnesses later testify in court, they are exempt; if they deny in court too, each earlier oath counts. A denial in front of the court is final, so the oaths that come after it add nothing, and they bring only one קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: they admitted, meaning they came and testified

phrases.aramaic: הִשְׁבִּיעַ עֲלֵיהֶם חָמֵשׁ פְּעָמִים חוּץ לְבֵית דִּין,
phrases.english: If he made them swear five times outside the court,
and they came to court and admitted, they are exempt.

phrases.aramaic: כָּפְרוּ – חַיָּיבִין עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת.
phrases.english: If they denied, they are liable for each and every one.
phrases.notes: They denied in court as well, so each of the five oaths outside court counts.

phrases.aramaic: הִשְׁבִּיעַ עֲלֵיהֶן חָמֵשׁ פְּעָמִים בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין
phrases.english: If he made them swear five times in front of the court
and they denied, they are liable only once.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִשְׁבִּיעַ עֲלֵיהֶם חָמֵשׁ פְּעָמִים חוּץ לְבֵית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the basic case of step 14 by asking what happens when the oath is repeated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repeated oaths outside court each count if the witnesses deny in court as well. Repeated oaths before the court count only once.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's reason: after denying in court they cannot take it back
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains why five oaths before the court bring only one קרבן. Once the witnesses deny in court, they can no longer go back and testify, so the later oaths do not hold back any testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: What is the reason? Since they cannot go back and admit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives the reason for the last rule of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A witness who has denied in front of the court cannot later change his testimony. So after the first oath, the next ones do not stop any testimony from reaching the court, and only the first oath carries liability.

keyTerms.meaning: to go back and admit, meaning to change their testimony

steps.whatToRemember: A denial in front of the court is final. That is why repeated oaths there bring only one קרבן, while repeated oaths outside court can each count.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: What is the reason?
Since they cannot go back and admit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: מָה טַעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the last ruling of step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one oath before the court counts, because after denying in court the witnesses can no longer retract and testify.

steps.title: Two witnesses who deny: together, one after the other, or one denies and one admits
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules on two witnesses. If both deny together, both are liable. If one denies after the other, only the first is liable. If one denies and the other admits, the one who denied is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If both witnesses denied together, both are liable. If one denied after the other, the first is liable and the second is exempt. If one denied and one admitted, the one who denied is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its rules for שבועת העדות. It now explains what happens when two witnesses deny at the same time or at different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A witness is liable only if his denial actually blocked testimony that could help the plaintiff. Once the first witness has denied, only one witness is left, and one witness alone cannot win the money case. So the second witness's denial does not really hold anything back.

keyTerms.meaning: They denied (claimed not to know any testimony)
Liable (here, to bring a קרבן for the false oath)
He admitted (that he knows, and testified)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the second witness is exempt because he lied less. He is exempt because after the first one denied, his testimony alone could no longer win the case.

phrases.english: If both of them denied together,
both of them are liable.
If one after the other,
the first is liable and the second is exempt.
If one denied and one admitted,
the one who denies is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּפְרוּ שְׁנֵיהֶן כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from Steps 14-16. It applies the same idea from רבי שמעון, that liability depends on whether testimony was really held back, to the case of two witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both deny together: both liable. One after the other: only the first is liable. One denies and one admits: the denier is liable.

steps.title: Two sets of witnesses who deny one after the other
steps.stepSummary: If there were two full sets of witnesses and they denied one after the other, both sets are liable, because the testimony could have been given by either set.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there were two sets of witnesses, and the first set denied and then the second set denied, both sets are liable, because the testimony can stand through either of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case that contrasts with the last one. Here there are two complete pairs of witnesses instead of just two people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the first set denies, the second set is still a full pair of two witnesses that could win the case. So when the second set denies, it also holds back real testimony and is liable. This is different from Step 17, where the second witness was left alone.

keyTerms.meaning: To stand, to be valid and usable

steps.whatToRemember: The test for liability in שבועת העדות is whether the denial held back testimony that could still work. A lone leftover witness is exempt, but a full second set is liable.

phrases.english: If there were two sets of witnesses,
the first set denied
and afterward the second set denied,
both of them are liable,
because the testimony can stand through either of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ שְׁתֵּי כִּיתֵּי עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with Step 17's 'one after the other' case. With full sets, the later deniers are also liable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two sets of witnesses who deny one after the other are both liable, since either set could have given valid testimony.

steps.title: שמואל: witnesses who swear before being asked are exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with שמואל. If the witnesses saw the plaintiff running after them and swore on their own that they know no testimony, they are exempt. They are liable only once they hear the demand from his own mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: If they saw him running after them and said to him, 'Why are you running after us? We swear that we don't know any testimony for you,' they are exempt, until they hear it from his mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ruling from שמואל about how the demand to testify has to be made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses did take a false oath, but nobody actually asked them to testify yet. They only guessed what he wanted. שמואל teaches that שבועת העדות requires the plaintiff himself to make the demand.

keyTerms.meaning: Until they hear it from his own mouth

phrases.english: GEMARA: שמואל said:
If they saw him running after them,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the man who needs the testimony, the plaintiff.

phrases.english: and they said to him: 'Why are you running after us?

phrases.aramaic: שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁאֵין אָנוּ יוֹדְעִין לָךְ עֵדוּת״ –
phrases.english: We swear that we don't know any testimony for you,'
they are exempt,
until they hear it from his mouth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: רָאוּהוּ שֶׁרָץ אַחֲרֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה. It defines the basic case from Step 14: the plaintiff himself must ask the witnesses to testify.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who swear falsely before the plaintiff himself asks them to testify are exempt from שבועת העדות.

steps.title: What does שמואל add? A משנה already exempts a request not made by the plaintiff himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל is teaching. A משנה already rules that if the plaintiff sent his servant, or if the defendant made the witnesses swear, they are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned: If he sent the request with his servant, or if the defendant said to them, 'I make you swear that if you know testimony for him, you will come and testify for him,' they are exempt,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל, asking why his ruling is needed. The quoted משנה continues, and the challenge finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That משנה already shows the demand must come from the plaintiff himself. A servant's message or the defendant's oath is not enough. If so, it seems obvious that witnesses who swear when nobody asked them at all are exempt, which makes שמואל's ruling look unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (his point seems already known)
He sent the request through his servant
The defendant, the one being sued
I make you swear (I put you under oath)

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned:
If he sent it with his servant,
or if the defendant said to them:
'I make you swear
that if you know testimony for him,
you will come and testify for him,'
they are exempt,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 19, saying שמואל's rule is already found in a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that witnesses are exempt until they hear the demand from the plaintiff's own mouth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already exempts witnesses when the demand came through a servant or from the defendant. That shows the plaintiff must ask personally, so שמואל's case seems to be already covered.
